statement: Bernoulli site percolation on Z^d, d >= 3, C(0) the cluster of the origin. Conjecture 1.4. Let d >= 3. For any p in ]0,1[, we have the implication theta(p, Z^d) > 0 => liminf_{n -> infinity} (1/ln n) ln ln (1 / P_p(n <= |C(0)| < +infinity)) > 0. [Context: Theorem 1.2 of the source proves that at p = p_c either theta(p_c, Z^d) = 0 or that liminf is 0; the source says 'it could be that the correct way to prove that theta(p_c, Z^d) = 0 is to prove separately theorem 1.3 and conjecture 1.4'.]
status_search: Source (Cerf, 2026-08-22) states it as a conjecture; the campaign ledgers carry theta(p_c) = 0 itself (C0023, C0094) but not this tail statement. No other search run.
title: Stretched-exponential finite-cluster tail wherever theta(p) > 0 (site percolation, d >= 3)

statement: Setting of the source's Part on pivots (Sections 47-58): for an increasing subset A of {0,1}^n, P^+_k(A, omega) is the set of pivots of order k of A at omega and phi_2(A) = sum_omega |P^+_2(A, omega)|, phi_{2 \ 1}(A) the analogous sum over second-order pivots that are not first-order pivots (formulas (51.1) and (52.1) of the source). Conjecture 53.1. Let n >= 1 be fixed. If A* is an increasing subset of {0,1}^n which realizes the maximum of phi_{2\1} or of phi_2, then { omega : sum_i omega(i) >= n/2 + 1 } is contained in A* which is contained in { omega : sum_i omega(i) >= n/2 - 2 }. [The source: the conjecture 'holds for n <= 7' by exhaustive search and 'yields a valuable upper bound' E|P^+_2(A)| <= 6 sqrt(n) for every increasing A; Section 59 tries Steiner symmetrisation and fails.]
status_search: Source states it as a conjecture verified only for n <= 7. Not in the earlier ledgers (no row mentions pivots of order two). No other search run.
title: Second-order pivotal maximisers of increasing sets sit between Hamming levels n/2 - 2 and n/2 + 1

resolved_by: Not a resolution: excluded because the source leaves the hypothesis class intentionally undefined (Section 58, PDF p. 437). Re-admit if a later version fixes the class.
statement: Conjecture 58.2 (Deviations pivotal inequality). Let n >= 1 and let p in ]0,1[. There exists a constant c = c(p) which depends on p only such that, for a decreasing subset D of {0,1}^n which is of the disconnection type, we have for all k in {1, ..., n}: P_p(D) <= exp( -(c/k)/n * E[ |P^+_k(D)| | D ]^2 ). [Source: 'Conjecture 58.2, if true, would imply that theta(p_c, Z^d) = 0'; 'the case k = 1 of these conjectures has been proved rigorously in proposition 39.5 and corollary 40.3'; and, crucially, 'so far we did not succeed in defining properly a class of disconnection events for which the conjecture could be verified, which is why this concept is left intentionally vague'.]
status_search: Source states it. NOT ADMITTED: the hypothesis 'of the disconnection type' is undefined by the source's own account, so the statement has no truth value until a class is fixed; recorded so that a later reader does not re-mine it.
title: Deviations pivotal inequality for disconnection events

statement: Bernoulli bond percolation with parameter p on a finite graph G = (V,E), o in V, B a subset of V. An event A is increasing with respect to the percolation configuration if omega -> P[A | pi = omega] is increasing on {0,1}^E (pi the configuration; the event may depend on extra randomness). Conjecture 2.2. There exists a universal function phi : (0, +infinity) -> R, independent of G, o, B and p, such that phi(eps) -> 1 as eps -> 0, and such that the following statement always holds. Let eps > 0. Let (E_b)_{b in B} be a family of events which are increasing with respect to the percolation configuration. Assume that P[E_b] >= 1 - eps for every b in B. Then P[ union_{b in B} ({o <-> b} cap E_b) ] >= phi(eps) P[o <-> B]. [Theorem 2.4 of the source: the conjecture implies theta(p_c) = 0 for every d >= 2, via Kozma and Nitzan's Theorem 6.]
status_search: Posted 2026-09-07; the source calls it its main conjecture. The earlier ledgers have no finite-graph connectivity conjecture (Kozma-Nitzan's is not there either, see G0005). No other search run.
title: Increasing-events boundary-connectivity conjecture on finite graphs (implies theta(p_c) = 0)

locator: proof of Theorem 2.4, Section 2, PDF p. 3 (restating Kozma and Nitzan, Conjecture 3)
statement: Bernoulli bond percolation with common parameter p on a finite graph G = (V,E). Conjecture (Kozma-Nitzan, Conjecture 3, finite constant-parameter form as restated by the source): for every eta > 0 there exists delta = delta(eta) > 0 such that, for every finite graph G, every A subset of V and every o, z in V, if P[o <-> A] > 1 - delta and P[a <-> z] > 1 - delta for every a in A, then P[o <-> z] > 1 - eta. [Kozma and Nitzan's Theorem 6: this implies theta(p_c, Z^d) = 0 for all d >= 2.]
status_search: Kozma-Nitzan's paper is cited by both Cerf (as [90]) and Flammant as very recent and unresolved. The earlier ledgers have C0138 (a different Kozma conjecture) only. No other search run.
title: Kozma-Nitzan high-probability connectivity conjecture on finite graphs

statement: Contact process with infection rate lambda on Z^d; lambda_1 the critical value for survival (lambda_1 = lambda_c on Z^d), and lambda_p the critical value beyond which the infected vertices of the upper invariant measure nu_lambda percolate. Source: '[8] proves in particular that ... lambda_p(Z) = +infinity, lambda_p(Z^d) <= 6.25 < +infinity for d >= 2. The same paper also raises the natural question whether we have lambda_1 < lambda_p on Z^d when d >= 2, which remains a difficult open problem. To the best of our knowledge, such a result has previously never been proven for any graph with lambda_p < +infinity.' The source proves lambda_1 < lambda_p on the regular tree T_d for all d >= 3 (and 0 < lambda_1 < lambda_p < lambda_2 < lambda_p^c < infinity for d >= 7).
status_search: Source (2026-09-09) calls it a long-standing open problem on Z^d. The earlier ledgers carry one contact-process row (E0007, two-type exclusion), not this. No other search run.
title: Is lambda_1 < lambda_p for the contact process on Z^d, d >= 2 (percolation of the upper invariant measure)

statement: Contact process on the regular tree T_d with upper invariant measure nu_lambda; lambda_p the percolation threshold of the infected set, lambda_p^c the threshold before which the healthy set percolates. Source: 'the figure suggests that both transitions are continuous, and it's possible as well that the probability to be in an infinite healthy component has a continuous derivative at lambda = lambda_p^c while the probability to be in an infinite infected component at lambda = lambda_p does not. We leave both questions as interesting open problems.' Question: are the functions lambda -> nu_lambda(0 in an infinite infected component) and lambda -> nu_lambda(0 in an infinite healthy component) continuous at lambda_p and lambda_p^c respectively, and is the first derivative continuous at lambda_p^c but not at lambda_p?
status_search: Source poses it (2026-09-09). Not in the earlier ledgers. No other search run.
title: Continuity of the two percolation transitions of the upper invariant measure on T_d

locator: Abstract and Introduction, PDF p. 1; Section 3, PDF p. 4
statement: Bernoulli bond percolation on Z^2 with parameter p. Source: 'on the square lattice is an open question to prove that the probability of the origin being connected to the vertex (0,n) is monotone in n' and, after the construction of a transitive graph without the property, 'it remains an open question whether graphs like Z^d satisfy the monotonic property or not'. Question: for every p in (0,1), is n -> P_p(0 <-> (0,n)) non-increasing on Z^2 (and on Z^d)? [The source traces the question to Hammersley and Welsh (1965) in first-passage percolation.]

title: Monotonicity of the two-point connection probability in the distance on Z^2

statement: Bernoulli bond percolation G_p on a finite graph G; lambda(G) the spectral radius of its adjacency matrix. Question 5.1. What natural conditions on G imply that if p >= (1 + eps)/lambda(G) then with constant probability G_p contains a component of size Omega(|G|)? [The source: 'the main difficulty ... is that lambda(G) can be governed by a very small part of the graph', with G possibly containing an induced subgraph H on (1 - o(1))|G| vertices with lambda(H) << lambda(G); the source determines the critical probability 1/lambda(G) for the emergence of a component of size comparable to the maximum degree.]
status_search: Source (2026-08-19) poses it. C0140 in the earlier ledgers is the transitive-graph giant-component question, a different setting. No other search run.
title: Conditions for a giant component in supercritical percolation on a general finite graph

statement: Bernoulli bond percolation G_p on a finite graph G with maximum degree Delta(G) and spectral radius lambda(G), p <= (1 - eps)/lambda(G). Theorem 1.4 of the source: a.a.s. the largest component has size at most O( sqrt(|G| Delta(G)) log|G| / lambda(G) ), optimal when lambda(G) >> sqrt|G| (e.g. K_{s,s^3}) but not in all regimes (for lambda(G) = Delta(G) and G connected the true bound is O(log |G|)). Question 5.2. For a graph with given Delta(G) and lambda(G), what is the tight upper bound for the typical size of the largest component of G_p, when p <= (1 - eps)/lambda(G)? The source singles out the near-regular case Delta(G) <= (1 + delta) lambda(G).
status_search: Source (2026-08-19) poses it. Not in the earlier ledgers. No other search run.
title: Tight subcritical bound on the largest component in terms of the maximum degree and the spectral radius

locator: Conjecture 5.3, Section 5, PDF p. 20 (restating Krivelevich-Samotij [28], see also [15])
statement: Conjecture 5.3 ([15, 28]). For every eps > 0 there exist d_0, gamma > 0 such that the following holds. If G is a graph of average degree d >= d_0 and p >= (1 + eps)/d, then G_p contains a cycle of length at least gamma d a.a.s. as |G| -> infinity. [Known: for d-regular G, Krivelevich-Sudakov give a path of length Omega(d) and Krivelevich-Samotij a cycle of length Omega(d); for average degree d and p >= C/d, [10] gives a cycle of length (1 - gamma) d with gamma -> 0 as C -> infinity; the source suggests combining its techniques with [10].]

title: Long cycles in supercritical percolation on graphs of average degree d (Krivelevich-Samotij)

statement: Conjecture 1.5 (Alon-Peres). For any eps > 0, there exists a C = C(eps) such that if Gamma is a graph on n vertices with all degrees at least 3, and k > C sqrt(n), then for any edge delta, the probability that a length-k random non-backtracking walk starting with delta is simple is less than eps. [The source proves the fixed-degree (regular) case; 'one could also explore analogs of these statements for (non-backtracking) closed loops'.]
status_search: Source (2026-08-28) attributes the general conjecture to Alon and Peres and proves only the regular case. Not in the earlier ledgers. No other search run.
title: Alon-Peres conjecture: non-backtracking walks of length C sqrt(n) are rarely simple (minimum degree 3)

locator: Conjecture 1.1, Section 1, PDF p. 1 (restating Catalano and Lavenant [4, Remark 3])
statement: Conjecture 1.1 ([4, Remark 3]). Let lambda denote the uniform probability measure on [0,1]. Then the diagonal and antidiagonal couplings (id,id)_# lambda and (id, 1 - id)_# lambda maximize the 2-Wasserstein distance from the independent coupling lambda (x) lambda among all elements of Pi(lambda, lambda). [The source proves the Gaussian analogue for all n: the couplings Law(Z, ..., +-Z) maximise W_2^2(gamma_n, .) over Pi_n(gamma), via the Gaussian isoperimetric inequality; the uniform case 'remains open to the best of our knowledge'.]
status_search: Source (2026-09-09) says open. Not in the earlier ledgers (no Wasserstein-dependence row). No other search run.
title: Catalano-Lavenant conjecture: the diagonal couplings of the uniform law are farthest from independence

statement: Threshold cascades of interacting diffusions on unimodular random trees, in the setting of the source's Theorem 2.1 (supercritical branching-random-walk representation with tilt parameter theta*, speed c*, derivative martingale dW_n). Conjecture 3.2 (Uniform integrability of the derivative martingale => Bramson delay). Under the hypotheses of Theorem 2.1, the derivative martingale dW_n is uniformly integrable (equivalently, dW_infinity > 0 a.s. on survival), and consequently the time-indexed front obeys F(t) = c* t - (3/(2 theta* c*)) log t + O_P(1), with the tightness and the limiting law of the recentred front given by a randomly-shifted Gumbel decorated point process, the shift being a multiple of log dW_infinity, exactly as for branching Brownian motion. [Source's Programme 3.3 lists the three ingredients, of which the x log^2 x moment condition for the offspring point process is the missing one.]
status_search: Source (2026-08-21) states it as the missing step of its Bramson programme. Not in the earlier ledgers (D0064 is the star-scale-invariance equation, a different object). No other search run.
title: Bramson correction for the front of threshold cascades on unimodular random trees

statement: Conjecture 7.2 (Continuous-type CRT scaling limit). Under the hypotheses of Theorem 6.1 at criticality rho(K) = 1, with the additional exponential-moment hypothesis on the offspring count (as in [1, Thm. 6.4]), the critical cluster conditioned on {|S| = n}, with graph distance rescaled by Sigma_c / sqrt n, converges in the Gromov-Hausdorff-Prokhorov sense to Aldous' Continuum Random Tree, with an explicit constant Sigma_c built from sigma^2_off and the tilted stationary law varpi*. [Source's Programme 7.3: the obstacle is that the type space is the Polish space R (or D x R), not finite, so Miermont's finite-type invariance principle does not apply directly; the missing input is a tightness estimate uniform in the discretisation mesh.]
status_search: Source (2026-08-21) states it. Not in the earlier ledgers. No other search run.
title: Continuum-random-tree scaling limit of the critical cascade cluster with a continuous type space

resolved_by: The source itself, Raphael Cerf, theta(p_c,Z^d)=0?, arXiv:2608.23661v1, Section 62 'The set of Talagrand', pp. 448-453: 'For a long time, we hoped that ... the maximum M2(n) was reached by sets which are little perturbations of A, or at least not too different from the upper part of the hypercube. ... Alas, Talagrand's example completely dashed this hope.' Running Talagrand's random CNF (Combinatorica 16 (1996) 243-258) with a coupon-collector second moment, it concludes (p. 453) P(|P2+(A,w)| >= cn) >= c for large n, so some increasing A has E|P2+(A)| >= c^2 n, against the bound E|P2+| <= 6 sqrt(n) that (53.2) derives from Conjecture 53.1. Proposition 62.1 as printed (M2(n) >= cn) omits the factor 2^n, and the derivation is loose about repeated coordinates; the conclusion and method are the author's.
